title: If you aren't using AI for image generation, for a 2d game without major/honestly near any movement animations, is there much of a need for the higher powered ones? I don't know where coding becomes this is too big for a older tier to handle
author: SoulstoneSpire
selftext:
I'm making a basically DMless DND game though it's evolved past just a tool for it ATP. There are a lotmof different aspects needing to be coded (I'm using SRD from WotC so I have to add every aspect of a class part by part to make sure it works) the only movement would be a character token moving on the combat field.

  
So far I've been using chatgpt with occasional use of their higher tier stuff because I have the 20$ plan, but I just wonder if there will be a point where I'll need to have regular use of it. Is Opus 5.5 even useful for me it seems very intense and expensive.

comments.author: BoringPossum
comments.body: The code quality always matters and unless you have 4090 or 5090 the local models you can run are slop. 20/month for ai is basically free considering how much work it gets done and you're making a product where human doing it would cost 120k/year

replies.author: SoulstoneSpire
replies.body:
I get the 20$ is cheap comparatively but my wallet disagrees in a personal level so it is what it is. I just wonder if there will be a point where the lower tier becomes functionally useless. 

Like I see people making like 3D assets and games and stuff, and I can understand needing the better ai for that, but if I'm not trying to get that sort of stuff in, is it less taxing or is it based on something else?

I am new to this I have a game in my mind that I want to play so I'm doing my best to address every time step one at a time to make sure things work how I want. I just have no idea what the limitations are haha 😅

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
the latest models can code entire games in days instead of weeks now.

if you dont mind working slow or you are still on AI-assist (some devs seem to wear that as a badge of honor now) then its fine.

you dont have to but you may as well take advantage of the tech available to you

with the latest AI upgrades, I am pretty much moving on from AI-assist at this point. maybe another 1-2 upgrades later then I just focus on art direction and design...

replies.author: SoulstoneSpire
replies.body:
First game and new to using AI so I'm being hyper critical about everything it's doing because well I don't trust it completely I had to use it for work purposes a couple years back and wanted to throw the computer off a cliff. It's absolutely terrifying how much better it's gotten. But I still don't trust it to just do what it says, gotta give pushback like you sure there bud? 

But I have no coding experience I'm on the I have art and music and a mental image of what I want and a stubbornness so go every single detail I can think of.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
AI from the last 2-3 months have been a lot better compared to how things were 1-2 years ago. 

honestly, we are close to a point where we can just prepare the spreadsheet, lore, characters, graphics and tell them to make a game. the latest models can take you like 80% there

especially since you have no coding experience, I would suggest keeping up with the latest AI models because the upgrades have been insane

like, I haven't had a bad experience with AI misinterpreting my prompt lately. When I run into typical AI issues with weaker models, I honestly can't even stand it now...

replies.author: SoulstoneSpire
replies.body: I had Astra look over my code sliced into like ten different types of reviews one by one (took surprisingly little overall weekly) then had the better Sol fix what she found. Well I'm currently doing so almost finished that. But Astra eats so much more than Sol omg 😱

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
you mean 6.1 astra? 6.1 sol is fine and it is stronger than 6.0 astra. 

yeah, astra will burn most of your 5hr limit in 1-2 tasks.

replies.author: SoulstoneSpire
replies.body:
No, Astra 6 is what they let you have use of for however much. And yeah it really does I'm glad I don't need to do that on a
 regular I just figured the game architecture had gotten pretty big and I should have it look harder at it. And honestly not much wrong I was pretty pleased with the severity and quantity of errors given the amount of added mechanics so far

I'll probably try to use Sol 6.1 more but the limits are annoying and I don't like having to wait to keep at it lol

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: yeah, my latest project ended up lasting 4 weeks due to limits. its fine, I guess, my projects don't usually make much if anything. no reason to spend more money to speed things up

replies.author: SoulstoneSpire
replies.body:
That's one thing I'm happy about. If I do publish it and it flops I still have the game I really wanted to play. Given how I want to review so many details even ignoring all the creative stuff I have to do it's still gunna make me a hot minute lmao. But if I want it to work how I want it to then I have to put in the work. 

God I have so much creative work to do but this is a mountain of my own making.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: yeah, hopefully the new models can make your life easier. that's why we are in this sub I suppose

replies.author: SoulstoneSpire
replies.body: Thanks for talking to me about this, I don't really have many I can talk to so much appreciation. Finally finished patching all the issues Astra found and now moving to fix the wolf bug :) damn that took a lot of five hour waits haha

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: feel free to dm me too if you like. I am usually online
